name: arm_fadvise64_64
synopsis: long arm_fadvise64_64(int fd, int advice, loff_t offset, loff_t len);
description: arm_fadvise64_64 is an architecture-specific system call on ARM that allows programs to advise the kernel about intended access patterns for file data. It functions similarly to posix_fadvise, enabling optimizations based on the provided advice.

parameters.name: advice
parameters.description: Advice about the access pattern for the data region

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting offset of the data region

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the data region in bytes

return_value.failure: Returns an error number on error

errors.description: The fd argument was not a valid file descriptor
An invalid value was specified for advice
The specified file descriptor refers to a pipe or FIFO

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.6, if len was specified as 0, it was interpreted as zero bytes instead of meaning all bytes through to the end of the file.
